# Copilot instructions — AutoShorts

AutoShorts is a **Tauri 2 + React 19 (TypeScript) + Rust + SQLite** desktop app that turns
long videos into vertical 9:16 shorts for Instagram Reels / YouTube Shorts.

**Full project memory lives in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) at the repo root — read it
before starting work.** It has the architecture map, the feature history, the verification
recipes, and the explanation behind every gotcha listed below.

## Must-know before you touch anything

### Frontend is one file

All React components live in [`src/main.tsx`](../src/main.tsx); all CSS is in
[`src/styles.css`](../src/styles.css). There is no `App.tsx` and no component folder — do
not go looking for one, and do not create one without being asked.

### API keys live in `.env` (repo root, gitignored)

DeepSeek, Deepgram, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq. The template ships fully
commented; only `LLM_PROVIDER=deepseek` is active. Keys must have **no quotes and no
spaces**. Keys are deliberately left commented out because `environment_status` uses
`std::env::var(...).is_ok()` and would report an empty variable as configured.

**Existing blocker:** onboarding cannot be completed on Windows with a DeepSeek key alone.
`handleCloudSubmit` in `main.tsx` requires Deepgram, `install_ollama` in `lib.rs` is
macOS-only, and there is no skip button. Workaround: a free Deepgram key, or devtools
`localStorage.setItem('autoshorts_onboarded','true')`. Do not "fix" this unless asked.

### Build commands need a PATH + vcvars preamble

`cargo` and `link.exe` are **not** on the inherited PATH. Every cargo invocation must
prepend the bins and call `vcvars64.bat` in the **same `cmd.exe` process**:

```powershell
$machine = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Machine')
$user    = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User')
$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.cargo\bin;$env:USERPROFILE\.local\ffmpeg\bin;$user;$machine"
& $env:ComSpec /c 'call "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat" >nul && cd /d C:\karti\my_working_dir\autoshorts\src-tauri && cargo test --lib 2>&1'
```

Harmless output to ignore: `'vswhere.exe' is not recognized`, `Blocking waiting for file
lock on build directory`.

### Verify with these

```powershell
npm run build              # tsc + vite — this is the ONLY frontend gate, there are no FE tests
cargo check --all-targets  # must be warning-free
cargo test --lib           # Rust unit tests
```

### The UI cannot be driven from a browser tab

`http://127.0.0.1:1420` renders but every `invoke()` throws `TypeError: Cannot read
properties of undefined (reading 'invoke')` — there is no Tauri IPC bridge outside the
Tauri window. To validate backend behavior, write a temporary Rust test and delete it
afterwards. That is the established pattern here.

### Verify a render by inspecting the artifact, not the log

Use `ffprobe` / `loudnorm` on the output. Expect 1080x1920, h264, aac 48 kHz stereo,
`r_frame_rate=30/1`, integrated loudness near **-14 LUFS**.

## Gotchas that have already cost time

**ffmpeg**

- `acrossfade` has **exactly one output** — supplying two output labels fails.
- **A dangling label aborts the whole `-filter_complex` render.** `has output N (label)
  unconnected` means the *graph label was never consumed*, not that the filter has an extra
  output. This was a real bug: `render_with_fade` always emitted an `[acat]` label, so when
  `keep_original_audio` was false crossfade silently degraded to hard cuts. Always guarantee
  a consumer for every label you emit.
- `-stream_loop -1` must precede `-i`.
- `amix` needs `normalize=0` or it halves volume.
- Silent audio: `-f lavfi -i anullsrc=channel_layout=stereo:sample_rate=48000`.

**Windows / PowerShell**

- No `&&`, `||`, `?:`, `??=`, `?.`. Use `;` and `if ($?) { }`.
- No heredoc — use a single-quoted here-string piped to `python -`.
- Write files BOM-free with `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $s, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))`.

**Repo noise — do not "fix"**

- `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` shows modified but `git diff` is empty (CRLF/LF artifact).
- `src-tauri/gen/schemas/*.json` are regenerated by `tauri dev`.

## Product constraints (do not violate)

- **Never auto-download "trending" music from Instagram or TikTok.** That is licensed
  commercial audio and scraping it is copyright infringement that gets users' accounts
  struck. Clip Mix Studio deliberately points users at their **own** music folder or a
  royalty-free library; the README and UI both say so. Deliver "trending ready" as
  production quality instead: fades, music balanced against voice, -14 LUFS normalization.
- No credentials in source — `.env` only.

## Working style for this repo

- Make surgical changes; the codebase is compact and well-factored, so read the relevant
  file fully before editing.
- Update [`README.md`](../README.md) when you change user-visible behavior.
- When you restart the app after changing Rust code, stop the specific dev-tree PIDs and
  confirm port 1420 is free first. Never kill processes by image name.
